method.selection: All incoming edges of each selected claim plus all incoming edges of each directly attached reasoning node; unique endpoint nodes. Closure computed by existing createRetrievalArgumentProjector, which validates graph via path expander.
method.denominator: 24 selected relation edges; 29 unique selected node occurrences including 5 claims. Missing-condition findings are separately enumerated and not added to either denominator.
method.source_access: curl GET /api/artifacts/{rootArtifactVersionId hash}; original PDF text read by page; rendered Table2 q90 and figures q30/q70 inspected. No nonpublic uploads.
method.boundaries: Source support means faithful reconstruction of what the paper reports, not scientific truth or external replication. Missing-condition search limited to the chosen conclusions and relevant methods/discussion pages.
method.excluded_inputs: No semantic assessment outputs, manuscript or review reports read. selection.json expected_answer was present and read; not treated as source evidence.
method.classification_unit: Node source-support classifications assess recorded_statement fidelity; scope/uncertainty, citation coverage and missing conditions are assessed separately. Relation classifications assess source-to-target inferential role, not independent empirical truth.

node_checks.recorded_statement: Mean grain size of sortable silt can indicate relative changes in bottom-current strength.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p9 explicitly invokes sortable-silt mean size as a relative current proxy, conditional on its strong positive relationship with sortable-silt content.

node_checks.recorded_statement: Hydrodynamic conditions around the Emperor Seamount Chain are stronger than in the open subarctic abyssal plain, especially at water depths of 1,000–2,500 m, as indicated by sortable-silt grain size.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p13 supports the comparative claim with its proxy qualifier; p9 limits discussion to pooled depth relationships because zonal depth coverage is incomplete.

node_checks.recorded_statement: The SO202 comparison for the open subarctic Pacific found a mean grain size of about 5.33 µm.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p9 gives ~5.33 µm for the SO202 comparison using the same end-member simulation method; this is not itself a calibrated current speed.

node_checks.recorded_statement: Water depth and grain size are negatively correlated in the study area (R = −0.74; Figure 5A), with deeper water associated with finer sediment.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p9 reports bulk grain-size/depth R=−0.74, distinct from the sortable-silt correlation.

node_checks.recorded_statement: The modeled surface-sediment end members had mean grain sizes of 9.12 µm (EM1), 64.95 µm (EM2), and 157.67 µm (EM3), representing fine silt, fine sand, and medium sand, respectively.

node_checks.assessment: PDF pp9,12 support spring-limited claim and absolute-value qualifier. NCA includes inorganic acid–base terms as well as organic contribution, so it must not be renamed pure organic alkalinity.

node_checks.recorded_statement: Based on absolute values, NCA was calculated to contribute approximately 32% of TA.

node_checks.recorded_statement: Extrapolating isotope-pairing denitrification rates over the western Indian continental shelf estimates annual fixed-nitrogen removal via denitrification at 3.70–11.1 Tg year−1; Table 2 reports the upper endpoint as 11.11.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p8 gives 3.70–11.1; actual Table2 p9 gives 11.11 and ±0.91; p11 prose gives ±0.91. Existing table-caption quote alone does not contain the cells, though actual PDF does.

node_checks.recorded_statement: The authors describe their annual estimate as almost three times higher than the previous estimate derived from changes in nitrate concentrations over time.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p11 explicitly says almost three times the prior nitrate-change estimate; Table2 p9 shows prior 1.3–3.8 versus present 3.70–11.11.

node_checks.recorded_statement: The prose and Table 2 give similar central annual denitrification-removal ranges, but disagree on the lower-end uncertainty and differ slightly in the upper endpoint.
node_checks.assessment: Confirmed from actual PDF: p8 lower uncertainty 0.091; p9 rendered Table2 lower uncertainty 0.91 and upper endpoint 11.11. p11 prose also gives 0.91, so the discrepancy is not uniformly prose versus table.

node_checks.recorded_statement: The annual range is an extrapolation from measured rates and assumed reducing-water volume; the authors' comparison to earlier nitrate-change estimates supports its interpretation as a substantially larger shelf-wide loss, while the uncertainty discrepancy limits precision.
node_checks.assessment: PDF pp8–9,11 support reported extrapolation and comparison, but its apparent precision must retain the p8/p9/p11 distinction and the rate-unit ambiguity identified below.

node_checks.recorded_statement: Applying the three-year mean denitrification rate to the estimated reducing-water volume over an assumed 90-day season converts incubation rates into a shelf-wide annual estimate.
node_checks.assessment: PDF p8 explicitly applies three-year mean 2.45±0.6 µmol N2/L/day to 1.2–3.6×10^12 m³ for 90 days. Reported annual magnitude is source-supported; literal N2-to-N mass conversion does not reproduce it.
